items.title: Building for the Agent-Native App Store (Ep.1042 with Salesforce’s Tyler Carlson)
items.summary: #Sponsored, SVP, Head of Product, AgentExchange and Partner Experience, Tyler Carlson, returns to talk to @JonKrohnLearns about building for an agent-native app store. Since Tyler’s last appearance in Episode 956, Salesforce has gone headless, opening its data, workflow and permissions infrastructure through APIs and MCP servers so that customers and partners can build their own personalized interfaces on top. AgentExchange now brings Salesforce and Slack apps, agents, skills, plugins, and MCPs together in one unified marketplace, built to serve human buyers as well as the AI agents searching on their behalf. Hear Tyler’s framework for the new software stack, how Salesforce tests skills and plugins across Claude, Codex, Cursor and other AI tools, and his advice for AI practitioners who want to reach Salesforce’s customer base in this Feature Friday. In this episode you will learn: • (00:00) Introduction • (01:19) Salesforce’s headless strategy • (07:49) How SaaStr runs on three executives and an army of agents • (10:17) Why AppExchange became AgentExchange • (20:47) Why skills and plugins are the new apps • (23:03) The Claudeforce partnership and testing across AI tools Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/1042

items.title: Revolut Cuts AI Costs 90% As It Runs Open Source GLM 5.3 On Its Own GPUs
items.summary: Revolut is cutting AI costs by 90 percent by switching to self-hosted models. Learn how this massive bank is shifting its strategy. Digital banking giant Revolut is moving away from expensive third-party providers to gain better control over its infrastructure. By deploying the Z.AI GLM-5.3 model on its own servers, the company aims to eliminate the high token costs associated with external API usage. This shift highlights a growing trend among enterprise tech firms looking to move beyond reliance on centralized AI providers. Beyond immediate savings, this move gives Revolut the independence to build proprietary AI models tailored to its specific financial datasets. The strategy provides a blueprint for other organizations struggling with the rising expense of large scale machine learning operations. items.title: How many "experts" are actually just getting their answers from AI?
items.summary: Anthropic gave 50 professional analysts an AI helper on a made-up farm task and secretly told the AI to favor one side. Most analysts followed it, and many repeated its arguments, sometimes nearly word for word. The lean was planted on purpose, so real life may look different. Still, none of the analysts surveyed suspected it, and that's the part that bothers me. If you hire an expert, would you want them to tell you when their reasoning came from AI?
